text: The per-service login is called 'the rwb-case login (DP-02)' in this story until the name is agreed; it owns schema rwb_case with read and write and holds no grant on the recovery.v_ace_* views, which only rwb_source_data may read.
why: The legacy story names no login and the per-service login name is fixed only at schema level, so the story needs a name to write its preconditions, authority and solution plan.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 (rwb-case: login rwb_case; schema rwb_case read and write; recovery.v_ace_* views SELECT only for rwb_source_data); Template and Rules v1 DP-02
confirm: Platform DB owner and ACE DB owner at the wave 4 environment build
impact: Documentation only; the schema and the grant scope do not change, and no ACE view is read by rwb-case.

text: gateway-bff serves SCR-45 as one composite route that calls the three rwb-case read operations in parallel with one hop each, a 2 s budget per call and a breaker per downstream, and merges the three answers into the screen model; the route path and merge rules follow the platform edge standard of RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
why: RWB-PLT-N001-CON publishes the composite route as a build dependency but no source document gives the SCR-45 route path, its merge rules or who owns its timeout.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 10 and 20 (gateway-bff: one hop, parallel calls for composite screens, 2 s timeout, breaker per service); Template and Rules v1 DP-19
confirm: Platform edge owner of RWB-PLT-N001-CON
impact: Screen composition only; no business rule and no data ownership changes

text: The reconciliation read (REC-01 to REC-05) and the business-key resolution read of the rwb-source-data contract are called as GET operations behind /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with the business date as a query parameter and a paged answer, alongside the published GET /freshness.
why: Architecture v5 slide 15 lists the rwb-source-data REST operations and names no reconciliation or key-resolution read, so the story cannot name the paths it consumes.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (rwb-source-data IN: GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}, /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId=, GET /freshness, POST /business-days/{date}/ready); FSD P1 v3 reconciliation of the case list to v_ace_account (REC-01 to REC-05); Template and Rules v1 DP-05 and DP-11
confirm: P1 rwb-source-data contract owner at the wave 4 contract freeze
impact: Contract shape only; the break and orphan values stay those the reconciliation produces

text: The three console read operations are published under the rwb-case service contract baseline (the OpenAPI 3.1 document already published by the rwb-case contract stories) and no separate contract story is created for RWB-AD-019.
why: The plan carries no CON slice for RWB-AD-019 and the story metadata records Contract dependencies as None, yet the story must publish three operations.
read: split_plan.json RWB-AD-019 slices (RWB-P1-AD019-APP, RWB-P3-AD019-APP, RWB-P1-AD019-OPS, RWB-ITG-AD019-ITG); Template and Rules v1 R5.7 rule 7 (every service has at least one CON story) and DP-19
confirm: TechX service contract owner and the wave 4 build sequence owner
impact: Adds three read operations to an existing contract; no new epic, no new dependency and no build order change

text: The stale set behind the console is refreshed every 15 minutes during the business window by a Temporal Schedule in rwb-case, with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window.
why: The story carries DP-10 and the workflow-kit dependency, but no source document gives a refresh cadence for a console stale list that reads the freshness of the data products.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (no shared Quartz tables; a Temporal Schedule in the owning service; JOB-05 timer check retired); Template and Rules v1 DP-10
confirm: TechX service owner with the data steward role at SIT
impact: Refresh latency only; the stale rows themselves come from the freshness contract

text: The rwb-case service runs as one login created with the rwb_case schema by the DB story (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-case login" until the name is agreed.
why: No source gives the login name, and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login.
read: RWB-P3-E2006-APP section 3, section 10 and the database notes of section 13; DP-02 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one login per service).
confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_case baseline is created
impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role in the story and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

text: SCR-14 reaches the case-side credit approval pack through a gateway-bff composite route that calls rwb-case, rwb-treatment and rwb-source-data in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model (DP-19).
why: The legacy story serves SCR-14 from one monolith endpoint; in the target the screen spans three owners and the composite route specification is not in any source.
read: Architecture v5 slide 10 (two calls in parallel, one hop each, merge at the BFF) and slide 20 (gateway-bff composes at most a few parallel calls); RWB-P3-E2006-APP section 12.1 and section 15.
confirm: Edge and gateway owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) with the screen design
impact: The pack is composed at the edge; rwb-case serves the case-side part and never calls another service on a user request.

text: The NLEADS credit decision is read through the rwb-source-data contract over v_ace_credit_decision and returns the NLEADS reference, the result, the approval level, the result date and the reason for a refusal, keyed by the plan of the treatment.
why: FSD P3 v4 makes v_ace_credit_decision the integration point and only rwb-source-data may read the ACE views, but no source gives the operation name or the field shape.
read: FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.33 integration points and change note; Architecture v5 slide 15 (P1 owns the ACE view contract) and slide 41; RWB-P3-E2006-APP section 12.2.
confirm: Source-data owner (RWB-P1 CON stories) and ACE, before wave 2 build
impact: The result record cites the ACE row instead of a re-keyed value; the field names may change without a behaviour change.

text: The rwb-treatment contract returns the plan terms of a RESTRUCTURE treatment and the legacy credit result columns nleads_ref, credit_result, credit_result_reason and credit_result_at, read by the case side and written only by rwb-treatment.
why: The legacy story reads and writes the four treatment columns in process; in the target they belong to rwb-treatment and the contract field names are not specified.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 11 (DF-TRT-023 to DF-TRT-026) and section 13 (the four new treatment columns); Ownership Map v1 (treatment and GET /treatments/{treatmentId} are S2); RWB-P3-E2006-APP section 11 and section 12.2.
confirm: Treatment owner (RWB-S2 CON story) before the S2 result slice is built
impact: The case side reads the result and never writes the treatment; a name change touches the client only.

text: The rwb-case database login keeps the service naming convention (schema rwb_case with one login) and is named 'the rwb-case login (DP-02)' in the story until the platform DB story fixes the name.
why: The legacy story names no login and the platform DB story has not fixed the per-service login names; the story must not invent a credential name.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 3 and 10; Arch v5 slide 41 and DP-02; TSD P3 v3 T5.2
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Platform DB owner and the rwb-case tech lead, before the first migration runs
impact: Placeholder only; no behaviour depends on the literal name, and the grant model is unchanged.

text: GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId} returns the treatment type, the state, booked at and the booking difference, and rwb-case reads those fields instead of copying any treatment row.
why: The legacy flow reads the treatment through the treatment interface, but the contract has no published field list for the booking fields the case side needs.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 11 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (DF-TRT-004, DF-TRT-012, DF-TRT-027, DF-TRT-028)
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 2
confirm: rwb-treatment owner and the rwb-case tech lead at the contract workshop
impact: A missing field adds one hop to the treatment contract or moves a fact into the confirmation event; the case never reads a treatment table.

text: The booking-match result passed to the rwb-case raiseTask activity carries the outcome (BOOKED, NO_BOOKING, TERMS_DIFFER), the accounts not booked, the difference terms and the message ID, matching the legacy TaskApi signature plus its facts.
why: The legacy story names the task interface and the two messages but publishes no result payload, so the activity input is a default read.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 4 steps 7 and 8, section 5, section 12 (TaskApi.raiseTask), section 14
applied_in: Section 12.5 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 5
confirm: rwb-integration and rwb-case tech leads when RWB-P2-E2007-CON is published
impact: A different shape changes the activity contract and its fake only; the task row and its messages stay as specified.

text: The case route-state move by R-RES-22 and R-SET-13 is evaluated in rwb-case on its own approved copy of package BOOKING_MATCH, as the legacy P3 module did, while the treatment state is applied in rwb-treatment.
why: The rule rows act on recovery_case.route_state, which rwb-case owns, but the Temporal and Drools design places the route sets with the route service; a ruling is needed so the story has one evaluator for the field it writes.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 4 step 6 and section 9; TSD P3 v3 T4; Temporal and Drools design slides 13, 15 and 18; Arch v5 slide 27
applied_in: Section 9 State transitions; section 12.5 Contract; section 13 Pattern application and Components
confirm: Architecture owner and both service tech leads during wave 2 refinement
impact: If the ruling moves the evaluation to rwb-treatment, rwb-case receives the decided target state in the confirmation and drops its rule client; the decision record and the outbox stay with rwb-case.

text: SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-01 My work are served by one gateway-bff composite route that calls rwb-case and the owning service in parallel, one hop each, within the 2 s budget, and merges the answers into the screen model.
why: The legacy story names the screens but no composite route, field list or masking detail; the screen has to be composed without a call chain.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 15; Arch v5 slides 10, 14 and 20; DP-19
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 12.1 Contract; section 15 Screens and states
confirm: gateway-bff owner and the rwb-case tech lead before the screen build
impact: The screen fields and masking are fixed later; the endpoints and the one-hop rule do not change.

text: The case-fact read returns one row per open case at the cut-off with id, caseNo, productGroup, status, stageCode, routeCode, queueId, entryDate, closedDate and totalCount, and the open case set of a business date is the recovery_case rows whose closed_date is null or later than the cut-off.
why: Legacy RWB-E2-009 section 12 names CaseReportingApi.caseFacts and openCaseCount without a response schema, and no source fixes the cut-off rule; the story cannot be built or tested without a field list and a cut-off definition.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-009 sections 4, 7 and 12; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (recovery_case DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023); FSD P3 v4 A1.5 and A2.18 (06:52 cut-off); Architecture v5 slide 15 (rwb-reporting projections)
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-reporting owner, before the case CON story is baselined
impact: If the shape or the cut-off changes, the read, the index and the AC2 and AC8 fixtures change with it; no case data is affected.

text: The per-service login for rwb-case is written as "the rwb-case login" until its name is agreed.
why: No source document names the database login of rwb-case; the story must not invent a credential name.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 (one login per service); Architecture v5 slide 8 (one login each); TSD P3 v3 T6
confirm: Solution architect and the ACE DB owner at provisioning
impact: A placeholder only: connection and migration configuration wait for the agreed name.

text: SCR-02 and SCR-37 are served through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls the owner services in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model; the SCR-37 route detail stays with the rwb-reporting owner.
why: Architecture v5 gives the composite route pattern and no per-screen route detail, and the legacy story describes the screen without a route specification.
read: Architecture v5 slides 8, 10 and 11 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19
confirm: Solution architect with the platform edge owner
impact: The rwb-case read is unaffected; the screen model and any field masking wait for the route detail.

text: queue_measure keeps the columns of TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030) and is written by the queue-measure story of RWB-E1-030; this story neither writes it nor fixes its dimension set.
why: The source defines the table but not the dashboard dimension codes, and the steering measures are rwb-reporting's per the ownership map.
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_measure; FSD P3 v4 A2.18; ownership map (measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish are P9; queue_measure is P3)
confirm: Solution architect with the data steward
impact: A dimension added later changes the queue-measure story, not this read.

text: The case facts reach rwb-reporting through the existing rwb.case.events.v1 event types that rwb-reporting projects, as Architecture v5 slide 13 shows; the 01:30 measure run counts the decision log entries of the day from the decision log, and this story's component tests stub that count and the published measures with the contract fakes.
why: The legacy story calls a P3 interface in process for the fact set and a P7 interface for the decision facts, while Architecture v5 slide 13 gives rwb-reporting only event subscriptions to rwb-case and rwb-decision; the target transport must be read one way and recorded.
read: Architecture v5 slide 13 (P9 row: listens to P3 and P7) and slide 15 (P9 IN: all business events as projections); legacy RWB-E2-009 section 12; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-reporting and rwb-decision owners; the ITG slice proves the wired behaviour
impact: No new event type and no new topic are needed; if the count must be pulled instead, the P9 story gains a C dependency and this story gains none.

text: rwb-case connects to ACE PostgreSQL with one login of its own, created for the service in the RWB-PLT-DB naming decision, holding DML on schema rwb_case only and no right on rwb_access or rwb_decision; until the name is agreed the story, the configuration and the tests refer to it as the rwb-case login (DP-02).
why: DP-02 and the service table fix one login per service and forbid the shared monolith login, but no source names it, so the connection and the grants cannot be written from the documents.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 (login per service) and R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one schema per service); Ownership Map v1 for the rwb_case tables
confirm: ACE database administrator and the platform DB owner at the RWB-PLT-DB review
impact: No business value changes: the login owns rwb_case only, so no approval, DoA or ledger row is reachable from this service.

text: The waiting-approval case and its decision task are served by the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, which makes one hop to rwb-case GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} for the status and route state and one hop to GET /api/recovery/case/v1/me/tasks for the decision task, plus one hop to rwb-decision for the approval summary, and merges the three answers into the screen model; the field list and the masking of the merged model are set at the RWB-PLT-N001-CON review.
why: DP-19 replaces the monolith screen with a composite route but no source gives the route, the hop list or the field list for a case waiting on an approval.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 20 and the gateway-bff notes; TSD P3 v3 appendix T-A API-P3-002 and API-P3-008
confirm: gateway-bff owner and the case service owner at the RWB-PLT-N001-CON review
impact: No screen behaviour changes for a user: the case still shows its status and its task; only the hops and the field list of the composite answer are fixed here.

text: ApprovalRequested and ApprovalDecided carry the approval reference, caseId, decision code, capability area, routed role, routed holder when there is one, approval level, limit version, due time, approval status (WAITING or HELD_NO_LIMIT), preparer user reference, and on a decision the final call with the rule ID and version and the resume state. rwb-case writes one task row with element_type DECISION_TASK, task_code APPROVAL, owner_role from the event, due_at from the event, status OPEN, and the approval reference and preparer reference in the assumed columns of the task shape; on a return it opens one task with element_type HUMAN_TASK and task_code APPROVAL_RETURN for the preparer. The approval level and the limit version stay in rwb-decision and are read back through its contract; no copy of the approval is written in rwb_case.
why: The case must open, own, reassign and close a decision task from an approval fact, and neither the event payload nor a task column for the approval reference is defined; the field names are copied from the approval and task definitions and the two task code values are the proposed defaults, not business values from a source.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 25 and 41; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 task DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026 and T3.2 LOV-ELEMENT; legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 4, 11 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09
applied_in: 4 Flow steps 1, 5 and 12; 7 AC1, AC2, AC9; 11 Data; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-decision owner and rwb-case owner at the RWB-P7-E2013-CON contract review
impact: If the agreed payload or task shape differs, the two activities, the migration column and the fakes change; the case statuses, the roles, the due times and every legacy value stay as they are.

text: While an approval on the case is open the case status is WAITING_APPROVAL, for an approval stored WAITING and for one held as HELD_NO_LIMIT; a held approval opens no decision task because no approver is named and the case still waits. APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED each return the case status to IN_PROGRESS; on REFUSED the route_state takes the resume state the routing rule named in the decision (for a settlement below the floor, R-SET-07 and DECLINED_BY_APPROVER_SET), and no case status is added to LOV-CASE-STATUS for either outcome. A case on hold keeps ON_HOLD and writes WAITING_APPROVAL to status_before_hold.
why: The legacy story says only that the case becomes Waiting approval or returns to the state the rule names, and LOV-CASE-STATUS has no state per approval outcome, so the status that accompanies the rule-named state has to be fixed for the case to be testable.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 9 and 11; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-CASE-STATUS and T3.1 recovery_case status, route_state and status_before_hold; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-SET-07 and R-UNI-42; FSD P3 v4 A2.3
applied_in: 4 Flow steps 7, 8, 11 and 13; 7 AC8, AC14; 8 BR14; 9 State transitions; 11 Data
confirm: Business lead and the rwb-case owner at the story review
impact: The status list is unchanged and no new status is added; the refusal keeps the rule-named route state, so the routing behaviour the business agreed is preserved.

text: An escalation of an open approval reaches rwb-case as ApprovalRequested republished for the same approval reference with escalation level raised by one, the new routed role or holder and a new due time, in place of a separate escalation event type on rwb.decision.events.v1. rwb-case treats it as a reassignment of the open decision task and of the timer row, writes no case status change and publishes no CaseStateChanged.
why: The approval escalates rather than stalls (BR7, R-UNI-30) and the topic carries ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided and RulePackageInForce only, so the representation of an escalation has to be fixed for the case to change its task and keep its status.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 (topic rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce) and slide 25 (ApprovalWorkflow); legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 4 step 9, 5 X1 and 9; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-30
applied_in: 4 Flow step 13; 7 AC2, AC11; 8 BR7; 9 State transitions; 12.4
confirm: rwb-decision owner at the RWB-P7-E2013-CON contract review
impact: The case keeps its status through an escalation, which is the legacy rule; if a separate escalation event is agreed instead, only the consumer mapping changes.
